This syndrome results from tumors, often neuroendocrine, secreting excessive serotonin. Serotonin is metabolized to 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), which is then excreted in the urine.

questions.prompt: A 34-years-old male comes to the outdoor patient department with complaints of episodic headaches, palpitations, and sweating. On physical examination, his chest shows pectus excavatum and a high extremities-to-body ratio. Growth is seen on her tongue, and a mass on the left flank is also palpated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: MEN 2B is characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas (growths on the tongue), intestinal ganglioneuromatosis, and a marfanoid body habitus with pectus excavatum.

questions.prompt: During recovery from anesthesia, a patient started experiencing hallucinations and vivid dreams. Which inducing agent is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Ketamine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that frequently produces dissociative anesthesia accompanied by vivid dreams, hallucinations, and emergence delirium during the recovery phase, especially in adults.

questions.prompt: A child visited the hospital with her mother with complaints of severe fatigue, lethargy, pallor, and irritation. She has a known case of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and is on oral iron supplements. On reviewing the child, the physician in charge plans to start IV iron supplementation. What is the next best test to be done in assessing this child?
questions.explanation: When assessing a child with known iron deficiency anemia (IDA) on oral iron supplements, who is now being considered for IV iron, serum ferritin is the best test. Serum ferritin is the most sensitive and specific indicator of total body iron stores. It helps confirm iron deficiency, assess the severity, and monitor the effectiveness of iron supplementation by reflecting iron repletion.

questions.prompt: A 40-year-old male presents with abdominal pain and progressive weight loss for 2 months. He has been suffering from migratory arthropathy for three years. There is no history of any chronic medical conditions. He is taking corticosteroids to help with the arthropathy. Endoscopic investigation shows dark staining of the duodenal mucosa. Histological examination of the biopsy using periodic acid Schiff stain reveals positive macrophages leading to a diagnosis of a rare multisystem disease. Which of the following statements is true regarding this patient's disorder? 1. Caused by a Protozoa Tropheryma Whipplei 2. PAS-positive macrophages in the lamina propria of the small intestine 3. Culture-negative endocarditis is a common cardiac presentation 4. Treated with IV Ceftriaxone
questions.explanation: Whipple's disease is a systemic infection caused by the bacterium Tropheryma whipplei (not a protozoan). It features PAS-positive macrophages in the small bowel lamina propria, migratory arthropathy, and can present with culture-negative endocarditis. Treatment involves prolonged antibiotics such as IV ceftriaxone followed by oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used for treatment of vitiligo?
questions.explanation: Psoralen plus ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy is a well-established and effective treatment for vitiligo. Psoralen, a photosensitizing agent, is administered orally or topically, followed by exposure to UVA light. This combination stimulates melanocyte proliferation and melanin production, leading to repigmentation of the depigmented patches. It is a common therapeutic option, especially for widespread vitiligo.

questions.prompt: A 45 year old obese lady with diabetes was managed with oral hypoglycemic agents. She now presents to the casualty with hypoglycemic agents. She now presents to the casualty with a hypoglycemic episode. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for her hypoglycemic episode?
questions.explanation: Glimepiride is a long-acting second-generation sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells independently of blood glucose levels, carrying a significant risk of causing drug-induced hypoglycemia, particularly in older or diabetic patients.

questions.prompt: If the diameter of an artery was found to be reduced to one-third. By what value does the resistance of the artery increase?
questions.explanation: According to Poiseuille's Law, resistance to fluid flow (R) in a tube is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the radius (r) of the tube (R ∝ 1/r^4). If the diameter is reduced to one-third, the radius is also reduced to one-third. Therefore, the new resistance will be (1 / (1/3)^4) times the original resistance, which is 1 / (1/81) = 81 times.

questions.prompt: A medical camp was set up on a military base. A 20-year-old military recruit is found to have an HbA1C level of 6.1% and fasting blood glucose of 120 mg/dL. He has no family history of diabetes mellitus and has no signs and symptoms of diabetes. General physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following best describes the blood glucose levels in this patient?
questions.explanation: According to ADA criteria, impaired fasting glucose (IFG) is defined as a fasting plasma glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL. An HbA1c of 5.7% to 6.4% also indicates prediabetes (impaired glucose tolerance/homeostasis).

questions.prompt: In a 13-year-old with acute flaccid paralysis, the pediatric resident orders an RT-PCR on a CSF sample to identify the causative virus. Which of the following described the enzyme correctly?
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by an enterovirus, which is a single-stranded positive-sense RNA virus. RT-PCR amplifies viral RNA by first converting it to complementary DNA using reverse transcriptase (an RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) followed by DNA amplification via a DNA-dependent DNA polymerase.

questions.prompt: A 35 year old man suffered a blow on distended bladder following which he developed sudden severe pain in hypogastrium associated with syncope. Later on as the pain subsided the abdomen began to distend. However he had no desire to micturate. Which among the following is true regarding his condition?
options: This a typical case of extra peritoneal bladder rupture
MRI is the ideal investigation to diagnose bladder rupture
Repair is done by suturing edges with single-layer 2/0 absorbable suture
Laparoscopic methos is avoided as it can be done only on laparotomy
questions.explanation: A blow to a distended bladder resulting in hypogastric pain, syncope, and subsequent abdominal distension without the desire to micturate is the classic presentation of an extraperitoneal urinary bladder rupture, typically associated with pelvic ring fractures.

questions.prompt: A young male patient presents with ptosis which reportedly worsens in the evening and improves in the morning. He also complains of excessive fatiguability towards the end of the day which improves with rest. Placing an ice pack over his eyes significantly decreases the ptosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of fluctuating muscle weakness worsening toward the end of the day and improving with rest, alongside ptosis improving with an ice pack (restoration of acetylcholinesterase activity by cooling), is diagnostic of myasthenia gravis. It is an autoimmune disorder caused by antibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

questions.prompt: A specific package of intervention and services which are given to population those who have either high risk of HIV or those who have reported high risk of HIV is known as targeted intervention. Which of the following group is not involved in this intervention?
questions.explanation: Targeted interventions under NACP focus on high-risk groups such as female sex workers, men who have sex with men, injecting drug users, migrants, and truck drivers, whereas doctors and nursing professionals are healthcare providers, not a target group.

questions.prompt: A 65 year old man presented to his primary care physician with a 3 month history of increasing urinary frequency without burning and nocturia four times each day. He has limited his fluid consumption and caffeine intake in the evening without much benefit. On prostate examination, the swelling was palpated with a smooth surface, firm, non-tender rubber like consistency was found. The physician thinks of benign prostate hypertrophy. All are characteristic features of benign prostate hypertrophy except:
options: J shaped/ fish hook proximal ureter
J shaped/ fish hook distal ureters
questions.explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causes urinary frequency, nocturia, and bladder outlet obstruction. Radiologically, BPH causes trabeculations and diverticula of the urinary bladder and upward displacement of the trigone/bladder base ('fish-hook' or 'J-shaped' distal ureters due to prostate enlargement), but it does not cause increased trabeculations in the bladder as an 'exception' because trabeculations are indeed a classic feature. Wait, let's re-verify options: BPH causes bladder trabeculations, J-shaped distal ureters, and can cause bilateral hydronephrosis if severe. Wait, distal ureters are indeed J-shaped; wait, option B says proximal ureters, whereas distal ureters are affected. Let's check: distal ureters are compressed by the enlarged prostate, giving a 'fish-hook' appearance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following side effects are seen most commonly with isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid)?
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin is a potent human teratogen (retinoid embryopathy) characterized by severe central nervous system, craniofacial, cardiovascular, and thymic malformations when exposed during pregnancy.

questions.prompt: You are a doctor in a village. A 1 year old child who is not taking feeds presents with fever and cough for 2 days. On examination, he is calm, with a respiratory rate of 51 breaths/min, and stridor is present. According to IMNCI (integrated management of neonatal and childhood illnesses). How is he classified?
questions.explanation: According to the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, a child aged 1 year presenting with cough and fever who exhibits a respiratory rate of 51 breaths/min (which is tachypnea for this age group, defined as ≥50 breaths/min for 12-59 months) accompanied by stridor is classified as having severe pneumonia, requiring urgent referral and parenteral antibiotics.

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old female presents with a complaint of abdominal pain and fever for the past 3 days. She localizes the pain to her epigastric area and states it radiates to her right upper quadrant. She notes that it became markedly worse after eating dinner last night. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. On Abdominal examination, Inspiratory arrest is noted on deep palpation of the right hypochondrium. Which of the following is the Investigation of choice for this condition?
questions.explanation: A patient with epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant, worsening after fatty meals, and a positive Murphy sign (inspiratory arrest on deep palpation) has acute cholecystitis. Ultrasonography (USG) is the investigation of choice.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old woman presents with severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia infertility and a diagnosis of endometriosis was made. The patient was posted for laparoscopy and at surgery dense pelvic adhesions were seen with bowel stuck to the fundus. Ovaries were cystic and stuck to each other. What is the next step of management in this patient?
options: Gestrinone to decrease the LH surge
questions.explanation: In a patient with severe, debilitating endometriosis, dense pelvic adhesions, frozen pelvis, bowel involvement, and completed childbearing (or severe disease unresponsive to conservative therapy), definitive surgical management consists of total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.

questions.prompt: A 23 year old G3 P1L1 A1 at 37 weeks of gestation with a previous history of emergency caesarean section and a dilatation and curettage presents to the ER with labor pains. During abdominal examination it was difficult to palpate fetal parts. Per vaginal examination revealed a 5 cm dilated cervix and her vitals were: BP-80/60 mm of Hg, RR – 20/min, Hr-106/min, SpO2 – 97% under room air. CTG showed a non-reassuring variable fetal heart rate pattern. The most likely diagnosis is—
questions.explanation: A patient with previous cesarean section presenting with labor pains, difficult-to-palpate fetal parts, vaginal bleeding, and maternal shock (hypotension, tachycardia) suggests uterine rupture. However, the exact prompt details align closely with classic signs of uterine rupture or placental abruption; review note highlights classic overlap, but historical key points to placental abruption or rupture.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old male child is brought to the ophthalmology clinic by his mother with complaints of blurring of vision for one week. The patient further explains that he only has blurring of the far vision and has no problem in his near vision. The patient gives a history of no other abnormalities. For a detailed examination of the eye, the doctor uses a short-acting topical medication which also has a cycloplegic effect. Which of the following drug was used by the doctor in this case?
questions.explanation: Tropicamide is a short-acting topical anticholinergic eye drop that induces mydriasis and cycloplegia for brief ocular examinations in children and adults.

questions.prompt: A young male patient sustained a right tibial shaft fracture following a road traffic accident. The patient’s right leg was immobilized with a plaster cast. This patient now presents to the emergency with severe pain in the leg. On examination, the distal pulses are absent, on passive stretching the pain increases, and on opening the plaster, the right leg appears edematous and numerous blisters are seen. Considering the suspected diagnosis, what would be the most appropriate management in this case?
options: Opening of the plaster is sufficient
questions.explanation: Severe pain, absent distal pulses, pain on passive stretch, and tense swelling following fracture and cast immobilization indicate acute compartment syndrome, which is an orthopedic surgical emergency requiring immediate fasciotomy.

questions.prompt: A 19-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of milk coming out of her nipples for the past 5 months. She is a nulligravida, and she is experiencing galactorrhea on a physical exam. She is diagnosed with prolactinoma. The characteristic physical finding of prolactinoma after galactorrhea is?
questions.explanation: Prolactin-secreting pituitary adenomas (prolactinomas) cause hyperprolactinemia, leading to galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and infertility. As the tumor grows suprasellar, it compresses the optic chiasm, producing the characteristic visual field defect of bitemporal hemianopia.

questions.prompt: A G2P1L1 lady underwent LSCS in previous pregnancy for fetal distress. This time she has an uneventful vaginal birth after caesarean section (VBAC) but the placenta could not be removed completely. The cord snapped on traction, but the placenta did not deliver. She also started to bleed more profusely now. What is the likely reason for this?
questions.explanation: A retained placenta where cord traction fails to deliver the placenta, accompanied by postpartum hemorrhage following a prior cesarean section, strongly indicates morbidly adherent placenta (placenta accreta/increta/percreta).

questions.prompt: A 29-year-old middle school teacher presented to the OPD with lower abdominal pain, laterally irradiated, and dysuria. In urine examination, eggs with terminal spines were seen. Eosinophilia was noted in her bloodwork. Computerized tomography (CT) scans revealed extensive calcifications of the urinary tract. A probable diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder was made on histopathological examination. Which of the following parasites lives in the bladder plexus?
questions.explanation: Schistosoma haematobium is a blood fluke whose adult worms reside in the venous plexus of the urinary bladder. Chronic infection leads to granulomatous inflammation, extensive calcification of the bladder wall ('porcelain bladder'), and is a major risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder.

questions.prompt: A 49-year-old male patient presented with complaints of achy swollen joints, fatigue, skin rash, especially on the face, and difficulty in deep breathing. Your senior resident doctor explained that it is related to immune competency and advised you to study the complement pathway. Which one of the following is a major component in the activation of the complement via an alternative pathway?
questions.explanation: The alternative pathway of the complement system is activated directly by microbial surfaces and relies on the spontaneous hydrolysis of C3, making C3 the central and major component in its activation and amplification cascade.

questions.prompt: A patient with a left-sided scrotal mass is being evaluated; the mass is found to be hard in consistency with irregular margins with no reduction on lying down or on manipulation and no cough impulse but with fullness in para-aortic lymph nodes. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A hard, irregular, irreducible scrotal mass without a cough impulse, accompanied by enlarged para-aortic lymph nodes, is characteristic of a malignant testicular tumor with metastasis. Primary testicular cancers present as painless, firm masses that do not transilluminate and lack reducibility.

questions.prompt: A patient presented with complaints of chest pain at rest for 6 hours and ECG suggestive of myocardial ischemia. Which among the following is used for diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) exists as five isoenzymes. LDH-1 is predominantly found in cardiac muscle and erythrocytes, making elevated serum LDH-1 (and its flip with LDH-2) a classic biochemical marker for myocardial infarction and ischemia.

questions.prompt: A young male patient was brought to the emergency department in an unconscious state after having collapsed at a railway station. As there was no pulse felt, cardiopulmonary resuscitation was started, and the monitor showed ventricular fibrillation. Immediate defibrillation was performed. What is the next step?
questions.explanation: According to advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) protocols, when ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia is identified and a shock is delivered, the rescuer must immediately resume high-quality chest compressions without pausing to check for a pulse or rhythm. Rhythm and pulse checks are delayed until after 2 minutes (5 cycles) of CPR.

questions.prompt: A 34-year-old male presented with a painless mass in the right inguinal region. On examination, there is a cough impulse on the index finger, and the swelling reaches done to the scrotum and reduces completely by pressing it through the deep inguinal ring with a gurgling sound. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A groin swelling that presents with a cough impulse, extends into the scrotum, and reduces completely upon manual pressure over the deep inguinal ring with a gurgling sound is characteristic of an indirect inguinal hernia, which passes through both the deep and superficial inguinal rings.

questions.prompt: A 42-year-old man presented to the ER with multiple knife wounds, one of which penetrated the right eye creating a 20 mm full-thickness laceration of the upper lid and a 12 mm superonasal full-thickness scleral laceration. The laceration extended radially back towards the optic nerve with prolapse of the intraocular contents. On admission, the patient underwent Evisceration of his right eyeball. Out of the given choices, Which layer of the eyeball is removed during evisceration?
questions.explanation: During an evisceration procedure of the eyeball, the contents of the globe (cornea, iris, lens, retina, choroid, and vitreous) are removed, leaving behind the outer sclera and the extraocular muscles attached to it.

questions.prompt: A 4 year old boy presents with low-grade fever, inspiratory stridor, and barking cough for the past 5 days. Examination reveals a hoarse voice, a moderately inflamed pharynx, and a slightly increased respiratory rate. His chest x-ray showed subglottic narrowing appearing like a steeple. Which among the following is not indicated in the treatment of this condition?
questions.explanation: The child's symptoms (low-grade fever, inspiratory stridor, barking cough, hoarse voice, subglottic narrowing on X-ray - 'steeple sign') are classic for viral croup (laryngotracheobronchitis). Croup is primarily viral, so antibiotics like parenteral cefotaxime are not indicated unless a secondary bacterial infection is suspected, which is not suggested by the prompt. Racemic epinephrine, helium-oxygen mixture, and corticosteroids (like dexamethasone) are standard treatments.

questions.prompt: A 50-year-old male was diagnosed with a submandibular gland tumor and underwent removal of the tumor following which the lingual nerve was found to be damaged. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: The taste sensation of the posterior one-third of the tongue is lost
The taste sensation of the anterior two-third of the tongue is lost
A general sensation of posterior one-third of the tongue is lost
A general sensation of the anterior two-third of the tongue is lost
questions.explanation: The lingual nerve provides general sensory innervation (touch, pain, temperature) to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, while taste sensation for this region is carried by the chorda tympani nerve (joining the lingual nerve). Damage to the lingual nerve thus results in loss of general sensation in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

questions.prompt: A 34 year old HIV-positive male presented with low-grade fever, cough, night sweats, and weight loss for the past 3 weeks. In view of TB investigations, the Mantoux test was negative, chest X-ray showed non-specific findings and an adequate amount of sputum could not be collected for slide examination. Which of the following is used to diagnose latent TB infection in this patient?
questions.explanation: In immunocompromised patients like those with HIV where tuberculin skin tests (Mantoux) can yield false negatives, Interferon-Gamma Release Assays (IGRAs) are the preferred test for diagnosing latent tuberculosis infection.

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old woman presented to the clinic with the symptoms of hearing loss and pulsatile tinnitus. Further examination reveals conductive hearing loss with the Rinne test negative. A reddish mass is seen behind the tympanic membrane. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?
questions.explanation: A reddish mass behind the tympanic membrane accompanied by conductive hearing loss and pulsatile tinnitus is pathognomonic for a glomus tympanicum or jugulare tumor. These are highly vascular neuroendocrine neoplasms arising from paraganglion cells in the middle ear.

questions.prompt: A man brings his father who became unconscious while working in a field in the host sun at 42 degrees Celsius in May. One examination, there were no physical signs of dehydration. His serum electrolyte values were normal. The physician found that the body temperature was 106 F. Which of the following symptoms is least likely to be seen in this patient?
questions.explanation: Classic heat stroke occurs during heat waves in vulnerable individuals exposed to high ambient temperatures, presenting with hyperthermia (temperature >104°F or 40°C), absence of dehydration signs, and altered mental status. A hallmark physiologic feature differentiating classic heat stroke from exertion-induced heat stroke is anhidrosis (absence of sweating).

questions.prompt: A young lady presented to the ENT OPD with a history of sudden onset unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, and dizziness following an episode of acute otitis media two weeks back. Rinne test and fistula test were positive. She had refused treatment then and currently came with complaints of worsened hearing loss in the affected ear. On examination, the fistula test was negative. What would be the most likely finding on the Rinne test in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Following severe otitis media with complications like labyrinthitis or fixation, mixed or sensorineural hearing loss develops. When severe sensorineural hearing loss occurs, bone conduction is severely reduced, but skull vibrations can still be perceived by the opposite healthy cochlea, giving a false negative Rinne test result.

questions.prompt: A 55-year-old female comes to the outpatient department complaining of fever, cough, muscle pain and headache. On taking occupational history, she reveals working for a centrally airconditioned corporate company. The doctor sent a sample for culture sensitivity. The microbiologist used buffered charcoal yeast extract to culture the suspected organism. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of fever, cough, muscle pain, and headache, combined with an occupational history of working in a centrally air-conditioned building, strongly suggests Legionnaires' disease. The key microbiological clue is the use of buffered charcoal yeast extract (BCYE) agar, which is a selective medium specifically required for the growth of *Legionella pneumophila*, the causative agent.

questions.prompt: A 10 year old boy rapidly develops hypoglycemia after moderate activity. Blood examination reveals raised levels of ketone bodies, lactic acid, and triglycerides. On examination, the liver and kidneys are found to be enlarged. Which of the following would be seen in excess amounts in the liver of this child?
questions.explanation: The clinical vignette describes Von Gierke disease (Glycogen Storage Disease Type I), caused by a deficiency of glucose-6-phosphatase. This prevents the liver from releasing free glucose into the blood, leading to severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia, and massive accumulation of glycogen and glucose-6-phosphate within hepatocytes.

questions.prompt: A 66 year old man presented with difficulty in urination, back pain, and an elevated PSA blood test. An x-ray revealed two radiolucent lesions in the bony pelvis and MRI revealed several enlarged lymph nodes in the lower abdomen. Which of the following drugs can most likely be used to treat the given condition?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of urinary difficulty, back pain, elevated PSA, and lytic bone lesions in an elderly male indicates metastatic prostate cancer. Treatment involves androgen deprivation therapy, which can be achieved using GnRH agonists such as goserelin.

questions.prompt: A 34 year old woman who was on a diet consisting predominantly of packaged and reheated meals presents with iron-deficiency anemia, painful and tender joints, and bleeding manifestations. Which of the following antioxidant deficiency can lead to these symptoms?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of iron-deficiency anemia, arthralgia/joint pain, and bleeding manifestations (such as petechiae and purpura) in a patient on a diet lacking fresh foods points to scurvy caused by Vitamin C deficiency. Vitamin C is an essential antioxidant and cofactor required for collagen hydroxylation and iron absorption.

questions.prompt: A 60-year-old female patient complains of pain and swelling in the left wrist following a fall on an outstretched hand. On examination, dinner fork deformity can be noticed. What is the most likely displacement seen in this patient?
options: Proximal and ventral displacement of radius
Proximal and dorsal displacement of radius
Proximal and dorsal displacement of ulna
Proximal and ventral displacement of ulna
questions.explanation: A fall on an outstretched hand (FOOSH) leading to a 'dinner fork deformity' is characteristic of a Colles' fracture. This fracture involves the distal radius, typically with dorsal displacement and angulation of the distal fragment. The term 'dinner fork deformity' describes the characteristic appearance of the forearm and wrist due to this dorsal displacement.

questions.prompt: A mother brought her 16-year-old daughter to the hospital with the complaints of primary amenorrhea. On evaluation axillary and pubic hair were present and other secondary sexual characteristics normal. USG showed absence of uterus. What is the next step in diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A 16-year-old phenotypic female with primary amenorrhea, normal secondary sexual characteristics (axillary/pubic hair, normal breast development), and absence of a uterus on USG has Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome or complete androgen insensitivity. Karyotyping is the next diagnostic step to distinguish 46,XX (MRKH) from 46,XY (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome).

questions.prompt: In a village with a given population, the total number of live births in a year is 4000. 40 newborns died within the first 7 days of life whereas 40 died due to various causes between 8 to 28 days of life. There were 50 deaths between the age of 1 month to 6 months of life and 0 of them died in utero. What is the neonatal mortality rate in this population?
questions.explanation: Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) is defined as the number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1,000 live births. In this scenario, neonatal deaths = early neonatal deaths (40) + late neonatal deaths (40) = 80 deaths. With 4,000 live births, NMR = (80 / 4000) * 1000 = 20 per 1,000 live births.

questions.prompt: A 22 year old primigravida at 10 weeks gestation comes to the ER with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Nausea and vomiting began one day back and now the patient is unable to tolerate fluids. She complains of pain in the right upper quadrant which started a few hours back. On examination, her temperature is 100.2 F, the pulse is 119 bpm and her BP is 110/70 mm of Hg. She has swelling of her lower limbs up to the ankles bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows a gravid uterus corresponding to 10 weeks of gestation and tenderness in the right upper quadrant, with mild guarding and is diagnosed as acute appendicitis. What is the next step of management? Complete blood count ● Haemoglobin: 11g/dl ● Leukocytes: 13,000 cells/µl ● Platelets: 150,000 cells/µl Liver function tests ● Aspartate transaminase (AST): 40U/L ● Alanine transaminase (ALT): 48U/L Urinalysis ● Protein: negative ● Pus cells: 1-2/HPF ● Bacteria: none USG abdomen: Reveals a 7mm diameter, aperistaltic, non-compressible, dilated, blind-ending structure arising from the base of the caecum.
questions.explanation: Acute appendicitis during pregnancy requires prompt surgical intervention regardless of gestational age. Delaying appendectomy significantly increases the risk of perforation, peritonitis, maternal morbidity, and fetal loss. Diagnostic confirmation via ultrasound followed by immediate laparoscopic or open appendectomy is standard.

questions.prompt: A 21 year old woman is brought in a drowsy state from a PHC with complaints of fever, severe lower abdominal pain, and purulent vaginal discharge. Her friend revealed that she had an unsafe abortion a week ago. On examination, her abdomen was distended, BP was 80/60 mmHg, PR was 140 bpm and RR was 36/min. Which of the following is not a causative agent of her present condition?
questions.explanation: Septic abortion complicated by septic shock is commonly caused by virulent pathogens associated with the female genital tract and unsterile instrumentation, including Streptococcus pyogenes and Clostridium species. Escherichia coli is not a classic cause of fulminant clostridial or streptococcal septic shock post-abortion, making it the correct exception among typical options.

questions.prompt: A 28-year-old male is positive for SARS-COV-2. A total of 30 people have been in contact with the patient and shows no symptoms or signs of COVID-19. What is the time duration for which they must be quarantined?
questions.explanation: When exposed contacts of an infectious disease such as SARS-CoV-2 require quarantine, the duration must cover the maximum incubation period of the disease to ensure that all infected individuals manifest symptoms or test positive before release.

questions.prompt: The adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells. These neural crest cells originate from the dorsal aorta. Clusters of chromaffin cells become the distinct medulla after birth. The adrenal gland first appears 28-30 days post-conception. Does the adrenal medulla secrete the following hormones?
questions.explanation: The adrenal medulla is embryologically derived from neural crest cells and functions as a modified sympathetic ganglion. It synthesizes and secretes catecholamines, predominantly epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine, in response to sympathetic stimulation.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of contact with COVID 19 comes to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of redness, photophobia, epiphora and malaise. Examination under strict precautions was done, however there was no blurring of vision or increase in IOP and fundus was normal. Which part of the eye can be most likely to be affected in this patient?
questions.explanation: Viral infections such as COVID-19 frequently present ocular manifestations restricted to the superficial mucosal layer, most commonly manifesting as acute follicular or viral conjunctivitis (affecting the conjunctiva).

questions.prompt: A patient who was in excruciating pain all over his body was taken to the hospital. In recent years, he has experienced these incidents frequently. When exercising vigorously, the ache begins. Anemia was detected on blood examination along with elongated RBC as opposed to concave ones. It was determined that he had sickle cell anemia. What substitution takes place in sickle cell anemia?
options: Substitution of valine by glutamic acid at the 6th position
Substitution of glutamic acid by valine at the 6th position
Substitution of valine by glutamic acid at the 5th position
Substitution of glutamic acid by valine at the 5th position
questions.explanation: Sickle cell anemia is caused by a point mutation in the beta-globin gene, resulting in the substitution of glutamic acid by valine at the 6th position of the beta-globin chain. This creates a hydrophobic spot that causes hemoglobin polymerization under low oxygen tension, altering erythrocyte shape.

questions.prompt: A research article is published about vasa brevia and its branches and course. Concerning the anatomy of vasa brevia, a first-year surgery resident is asked a question by a senior surgeon; the question appears like vasa brevia is the other name for which of the following arteries is carried by the gastrosplenic ligament.
questions.explanation: The vasa brevia are alternate anatomical names for the short gastric arteries, which travel within the gastrosplenic ligament to supply the gastric fundus.

questions.prompt: A young sexually active female patient presented to the outpatient department with complaints of lower abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge. On examination, the body temperature is 103 degrees Fahrenheit, pulse rate is 109 per minute and there is abdominal tenderness. Cervical motion tenderness is present on examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of lower abdominal pain, fever, high pulse rate, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and cervical motion tenderness in a young sexually active female is classic for pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Cervical motion tenderness is a cardinal sign of upper genital tract infection.

questions.prompt: A 32-year-old male with a history of peptic ulcer disease and diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency with a complaint of nausea, abdominal pain and lethargy for 2 days. He reports having occasional dark, tarry stools. Laboratory investigations reveal elevated blood glucose and a high anion gap metabolic acidosis on an arterial blood gas sample. Which of the following types of insulin should be used in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: In the management of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) presenting with severe hyperglycemia and high anion gap metabolic acidosis, intravenous regular insulin is the treatment of choice due to its rapid onset and predictable half-life.

questions.prompt: A 25 year old female presented previous history of chlamydia infection now presents with low-grade fever and non-specific lower abdominal pain. Examination reveals mild diffuse lower abdominal tenderness on deep palpation, cervical motion tenderness, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. What are the long-term sequelae of this condition?
questions.explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) resulting from sexually transmitted infections like Chlamydia trachomatis causes chronic fallopian tube inflammation, leading to tubal scarring, adhesion formation, and a significantly increased risk of tubal factor infertility.

questions.prompt: A mother complains of cramps in her breasts while breastfeeding her child. Which hormone is responsible for this?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is a neurohypophysial hormone responsible for the milk ejection reflex ('let-down reflex') during lactation. It causes contraction of the myoepithelial cells surrounding the mammary alveoli, which produces breast cramps or a tingling sensation and forces milk into the ducts.

questions.prompt: A woman at 36 weeks of pregnancy, with a history of a previous C-section, presents with symptoms of low blood pressure, tachycardia, and fluid in the peritoneum on ultrasound. What is the likely diagnosis, and what would be the appropriate next steps in management?
questions.explanation: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks with a prior C-section presenting with acute abdominal pain, hypotension, tachycardia, and intraperitoneal fluid has signs of uterine scar rupture, requiring emergency exploratory laparotomy.

questions.prompt: A 20 year old male presented with a 1 week history of yellow skin and sclerae but is otherwise asymptomatic. He gives a history of viral infection 10 days ago which was resolved 2 days back. There is a history of a similar episode of icterus 2 years back when the patient had long hours of basketball practice. The current serum bilirubin is 2.4 mg/dl, unconjugated bilirubin is 2.1mg/dl, and conjugated bilirubin is 0.3mg/dl. Serum AST and ALT levels are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This young male exhibits intermittent, mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia triggered by stress (basketball practice) and minor illness, with otherwise normal liver enzymes and complete absence of hemolysis. This presentation is classic for Gilbert syndrome, caused by a benign reduction in UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity.

questions.prompt: A researcher is studying the difference in the incidence of asthma in children who are exposed to second-hand smoke and those who are not. If he wishes to express the additional incidence of asthma in the exposed children as a percentage, which of the following should he use?
questions.explanation: Attributable risk (risk difference) measures the absolute amount of disease incidence in the exposed group that can be attributed to the exposure, often expressed as a percentage or excess rate compared to the unexposed group.

questions.prompt: Miss. Uma presents to you with complaints of mass descending per vaginum for the past 6 months. On examination, you notice a grade 3 uterovaginal prolapse and a decubitus ulcer over the prolapse. Which of the following is a cause for this decubitus ulcer and treatment?
options: Venous congestion and reduction of the prolapsed part into the vagina and daily packing with glycerine and acriflavine
questions.explanation: Decubitus ulcers associated with advanced uterine prolapse are primarily caused by chronic friction, trauma, and impaired venous congestion from the exposed prolapsed tissues protruding outside the vagina. Treatment involves gentle reduction of the prolapse back into the vaginal vault, daily antiseptic packing (e.g., glycerine and acriflavine), and optimizing mucosal health prior to definitive surgical repair.

questions.prompt: A 60-year-old male presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. On examination, the right ear reveals conductive hearing loss with a dull tympanic membrane. Moreover, decreased mobility of the soft palate was also noted. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) often presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy as a common initial symptom due to its rich lymphatic drainage. Other classic signs include conductive hearing loss (due to eustachian tube obstruction by the tumor), and cranial nerve palsies (like decreased soft palate mobility) due to local tumor extension. The combination of these symptoms strongly suggests NPC.

questions.prompt: A 24-year-old female patient presented with malar rash, recurrent oral ulcers, and multiple joint pain. She has no relevant past history and does not take any medication. On further investigations, thrombocytopenia was seen and the Anti-Sm antibody was positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?
questions.explanation: The clinical triad of malar rash, oral ulcers, and polyarthralgia combined with thrombocytopenia and positive Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies is diagnostic of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Anti-Sm antibody is highly specific for SLE.

questions.prompt: A 54-year-old female presents to the surgical outpatient department with the complaint of rapidly increasing central neck swelling over the last 4 weeks. It is associated with weight loss, anorexia, and a change in voice character but not with dysphagia. Her mother had a similar neck swelling and was diagnosed with thyroid cancer. Her pulse rate is 100/min, BP is 120/80, respiratory rate is 14/min, and temperature is 98.6° F. Examination reveals a hard nodule over the neck that moves with swallowing; however, there were no palpable lymph nodes. Based on her history and clinical examination, which type of thyroid cancer might she suffer from?
questions.explanation: A rapidly growing, hard thyroid nodule with local invasion (change in voice) and a family history of thyroid cancer in an older patient strongly points toward follicular or anaplastic thyroid carcinoma. Follicular carcinoma is characterized by vascular/capsular invasion and hematogenous spread.

questions.prompt: A 70-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with a recurrent stroke after he was found unconscious by his neighbour on the floor of his apartment. He has a history of cerebrovascular disease. On examination, he was found to have an unusual breathing pattern. Which of the following breathing patterns have prolonged inspiratory spasms that resemble breath-holding?
questions.explanation: Apneustic breathing is an abnormal respiratory pattern characterized by prolonged inspiratory gasps or pauses (sustained inspiration) followed by brief expiration, typically resulting from damage to the pontine respiratory center (lower pons).

questions.prompt: A 30 year old lady met with a road traffic accident, she didn’t wear her helmet, she had loss of consciousness for some minutes and then she became normal, after 2 days, she rushed to ENT department complaining clear fluid discharge from nose, what could be the diagnosis?
options: Infection due to hemosinus because of RTA
questions.explanation: Post-traumatic clear fluid discharge from the nose following head injury and a transient loss of consciousness is characteristic of CSF rhinorrhea. This occurs due to a fracture of the anterior cranial fossa (cribriform plate of ethmoid or frontal sinus) tearing the dura mater and arachnoid.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements are true about tremors? 1. PD is characterized by resting tremor 2. Tremor consist of alternate contraction of agonist and antagonist muscle in an oscillating rhythmic manner 3. Essential tremor is an uncommon movement disorder affecting 5% of the population 4. Normal individuals can have physiologic tremors that manifest as mild high frequency, postural or action tremors
questions.explanation: Parkinson's disease is characterized by a resting tremor (statement 1). Tremors consist of rhythmic, alternating contractions of agonist and antagonist muscles (statement 2). Essential tremor is common, affecting up to 5% of older adults, making statement 3 incorrect. Physiologic tremors are normal, high-frequency postural/action tremors (statement 4).

questions.prompt: A patient underwent a left submandibular gland excision during which the hypoglossal nerve was injured. Which of the following deficits would be seen in this case?
options: Deviated tongue to the contralateral side
Deviated tongue to the same side
Loss of taste in posterior 1/3rd of the tongue
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) innervates all intrinsic and most extrinsic muscles of the tongue, primarily responsible for tongue movement. If the hypoglossal nerve is injured, the ipsilateral (same side) tongue muscles will be paralyzed and atrophy. When the patient attempts to protrude the tongue, the unopposed action of the healthy contralateral genioglossus muscle will cause the tongue to deviate towards the side of the lesion/injury.

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old boy has been observed by his parents to be increasingly clumsy for the past 6 months. On physical examination, there is a cauliflower-like growth in the left eye alongside leukocoria and an absent red reflex. A diagnosis was made and enucleation was done. The microscopic appearance of the specimen shows Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), an absent red reflex, and a cauliflower-like growth in the eye of a 3-year-old boy is highly suggestive of retinoblastoma. The definitive diagnosis is confirmed by the microscopic finding of Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes, which are pathognomonic for retinoblastoma, a malignant tumor of the retina.

questions.prompt: A patient diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma is found to have a tumor that is 10 cm in size, situated at the lower pole of the kidney with negative regional lymph nodes. Which of the following is the preferred management for this patient?
questions.explanation: For localized renal cell carcinoma, radical nephrectomy is the traditional standard of care when the tumor is large (such as 10 cm) or anatomically complex, precluding safe partial nephrectomy. Although partial nephrectomy is preferred for small, localized masses to preserve renal function, larger tumors or those invading beyond local boundaries generally necessitate radical nephrectomy.

questions.prompt: A child with mental retardation, blindness, and muscle weakness was investigated and was found to be deficient for Hexosaminidase-A enzyme. She is most likely suffering from..
questions.explanation: Tay-Sachs disease is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by a deficiency of the Hexosaminidase-A enzyme, resulting in GM2 ganglioside accumulation and presenting with mental retardation, blindness, and muscle weakness (along with cherry-red spots).

questions.prompt: A patient presented with complaints of fever for 3 days and general fatigue. On examination, splinter hemorrhages were seen. Echocardiography revealed vegetations on the valves and thus a blood culture as done. The organism in the culture was seen as cocci in chains that showed alpha hemolysis on blood agar and was resistant to optochin and bile. Which of the following bacteria is most commonly implicated in this condition?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus sanguis (part of the viridans group streptococci) is a prominent cause of subacute infective endocarditis, especially in patients with dental caries or underlying valvular disease. Microbiologically, it consists of gram-positive cocci in chains, exhibits alpha-hemolysis on blood agar, and is distinguished from Streptococcus pneumoniae by being resistant to optochin and unable to ferment inulin (bile-esculin variable, but optochin resistant).

questions.prompt: During the examination of a victim of assault, you notice a wound with ragged, irregular, and uneven margins with tears diverging at an angle from the end of the main wound and typical swallowtails. Bleeding from this wound is not significant and shows crushed blood vessels and hair bulbs. You would document this wound as a/an.
questions.explanation: Lacerated wounds are caused by blunt force trauma, leading to tearing of tissues. Their characteristic features include ragged, irregular, and uneven margins, often with 'swallowtails' (small tears diverging from the main wound). Bleeding is typically not significant due to crushed blood vessels, and hair bulbs may be crushed, distinguishing them from sharp force injuries.

questions.prompt: A male patient complained of imbalance, numbness of the foot, and muscle weakness. On history taking, he revealed that he has been taking multivitamin tablets more than the prescribed dose for 1 year. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the associated symptoms seen in this patient?
questions.explanation: Excessive intake of pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) supplements over a prolonged period leads to sensory neuropathy, manifesting as ataxia, numbness of the feet, and muscle weakness, mimicking dorsal column dysfunction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would help in explaining the mechanism of action of ANP (atrial natriuretic peptide)?
questions.explanation: Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) exerts its effects by binding to specific guanylyl cyclase receptors on target cells. This binding activates the enzyme, leading to an increase in the intracellular concentration of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP), which acts as a secondary messenger to mediate ANP's physiological actions, such as vasodilation and natriuresis.

questions.prompt: A 14-year-old male presented with recurrent epistaxis. There is no history of trauma associated with it. He also complained of nasal obstruction and rhinorrhea. On examination, there is a firm purplish mass on the posterior nasopharynx. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A young male adolescent presenting with recurrent epistaxis, nasal obstruction, and a firm, purplish vascular mass in the nasopharynx has classic juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA).

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old man presents to the casualty with a sudden loss of vision and painful ocular movements. On examination of the affected eye, a relative afferent pupillary defect with a normal optic disc is seen. Visual field testing was done which revealed a central scotoma in the same eye. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Optic neuritis classically presents in young to middle-aged adults with acute, painful unilateral loss of vision, often associated with pain on eye movement. Examination typically reveals a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) and a normal optic disc (retrobulbar neuritis), though papillitis can also occur. Visual field testing commonly demonstrates a central or centrocecal scotoma. It is frequently linked with demyelinating disease like multiple sclerosis.

questions.prompt: There is a group of 200 hypertensive patients. First group of 100 patients is given medical advice whereas a second group of 100 patients is advised lifestyle changes. Which of the following tests of significance is used to compare the blood pressure after 3 months?
questions.explanation: To compare the mean blood pressure of two independent groups of patients (medical advice group versus lifestyle changes group) after an intervention, the unpaired t-test is the appropriate statistical test of significance for normally distributed continuous variables.

questions.prompt: A 39-year-old male presents to the clinic for a routine checkup. Except for the mild generalized weakness, he does not have any symptoms. On assessment following findings are noted. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the above findings? Parameters Values ALP Normal Calcium High Phosphate High PTH Normal
questions.explanation: In Vitamin D toxicity, excessive vitamin D leads to increased intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption, resulting in hypercalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. Due to suppressed parathyroid hormone (PTH) via negative feedback from high calcium levels and normal alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in uncomplicated toxicity, this metabolic profile points directly to Vitamin D intoxication.

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old female comes to the OPD for well-care visits. The patient is completely well and eats a balanced diet. She never smokes or drinks alcohol and has no significant past medical history. On examination, her vitals are normal. The patient tells the physician that next week she will go on a trip to an island and is worried about motion sickness. Which of the following drugs may be considered first-line therapy for this patient's prophylaxis of motion sickness?
questions.explanation: For prophylaxis of motion sickness, antihistamines with anticholinergic properties are considered first-line. Promethazine, a first-generation H1 antihistamine, is highly effective due to its potent anticholinergic and sedative effects, which help to suppress vestibular stimulation and the vomiting center. It should be taken before travel for optimal effect. Other options are generally not first-line for prophylaxis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about GFR? GFR-Glomerular filtration rate RPF-Renal Plasma Flow
options: An increase in sympathetic function increases GFR
An increase in RPF increases GFR
A decrease in RPF increases GFR
questions.explanation: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is directly proportional to renal plasma flow (RPF), assuming other factors like filtration fraction and glomerular capillary pressure remain constant. An increase in RPF delivers more plasma to the glomeruli, thus increasing the volume of fluid filtered. Conversely, a decrease in RPF would decrease GFR.

questions.prompt: The students of a boarding school eat from the same canteen. One of the students developed abdominal pain, jaundice, and fever following which other students also presented with similar symptoms. Which of the following investigations should the medical officer of the area check for to reach a diagnosis?
questions.explanation: An outbreak of acute abdominal pain, jaundice, and fever in a boarding school canteen setting strongly points to a common-source waterborne or foodborne outbreak of Hepatitis A virus. Diagnosis of acute hepatitis A infection is confirmed by detecting anti-Hepatitis A virus IgM antibodies.

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old female complains of increased anxiety and repetitive thoughts of her hands being contaminated and engages in repeated washing of her hands. Her thoughts are distressing but she is not able to overcome them. If she tries to hold herself from washing, it further aggravates her anxiety. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by the presence of persistent, intrusive, distressing thoughts, images, or impulses (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed to reduce associated anxiety (compulsions). The patient's fear of contamination coupled with repetitive hand washing constitutes classic OCD.

questions.prompt: An industrial worker was admitted to the hospital after an eye injury sustained while cutting stone with a hammer and iron chisel. A foreign body was suspected to be impacted in his eye. Which of the following is the best investigation for foreign body localization?
questions.explanation: Computed tomography (CT) scan is the gold standard and best imaging investigation for localizing intraocular metallic or stone foreign bodies following trauma.

questions.prompt: A surveyor visits a household consisting of a 35-year-old man, his wife who is 6 weeks pregnant and a 3-year-old child. The man's brother along with his wife is currently visiting them for a month owing to winter vacation. What type of family would the surveyor classify the household?
questions.explanation: A nuclear family is defined as a household consisting of a married couple and their children. Even though temporary visitors (the brother and his wife) are staying for a month, the core residential unit remains the man, his wife, and their child, classifying it as a nuclear family.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old boy fell from the bed and developed nose swelling and difficulty breathing. Examination revealed smooth rounded swellings on either side of the septum through both nares. On palpation, it was soft and fluctuant. What is the next best step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Nasal trauma resulting in a soft, fluctuant, bilateral swelling of the nasal septum indicates a nasal septal hematoma, which requires urgent incision and drainage to prevent septal cartilage necrosis and saddle nose deformity.

questions.prompt: A patient has lost sensation over the dorsum of the foot and medial 4 toes. There is the associated difficulty of eversion of the foot. Which nerve injury is likely to be the reason for this
questions.explanation: The superficial peroneal nerve supplies the muscles of the lateral compartment of the leg (peroneus longus and brevis) responsible for foot eversion, and provides sensory innervation to the dorsum of the foot and medial four toes. Injury to this nerve leads to eversion weakness and dorsal foot numbness.

questions.prompt: You are an intern, posted in the neurology ward in the Department of Internal Medicine. A 48- year-old woman was admitted with a history of muscle weakness. Investigations & examination revealed normal nerve conduction but flaccidity is seen. Which of the following would be the possible diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder characterized by fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigability. It involves antibodies attacking acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, leading to impaired signal transmission. Crucially, nerve conduction studies are typically normal because the nerves themselves are unaffected, while muscle weakness and flaccidity result from defective neuromuscular transmission.

questions.prompt: A stable 25 years old farmer was admitted with acute onset of fever, cough, and dyspnea. Chest radiograph showed findings of pneumonia for which he was treated with antibiotics; showed good response. After 1 month he again presented in the hypoxemic state with progressive dyspnea. CT chest showed diffuse ground glass changes. Transbronchial biopsies showed numerous small granulomas and marked lymphocytosis. Which of the following is a causative agent for a given disease?
questions.explanation: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis) occurs due to repeated inhalation of organic antigens, such as thermophilic actinomycetes found in moldy hay (farmer's lung). It presents subacutely or chronically with dyspnea, lymphocytic alveolitis, and non-caseating granulomas.

questions.prompt: A 50 year old man presents with recurrent episodes of chest pain which is seen only on exertion or exercise and lasts 2-5 minutes. He was assessed and was diagnosed with a case of stable angina however his BP was consistently elevated. What is the most appropriate antihypertensive for this patient?
questions.explanation: In stable angina accompanied by hypertension, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers like amlodipine are excellent antihypertensive agents because they reduce peripheral vascular resistance and myocardial oxygen demand without worsening coronary perfusion.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the causative agent for acne fulminans?
questions.explanation: Acne fulminans is a severe, rare, and ulcerative form of acne vulgaris characterized by sudden onset, systemic symptoms (such as fever and polyarthralgia), and hemorrhagic crusting. The condition is strongly associated with an exaggerated immune response to antigens from Cutibacterium acnes (formerly classified as Propionibacterium acnes), an anaerobic bacterium residing in sebaceous follicles.

questions.prompt: A 7-year-old female child is brought to the OPD with cramping abdominal pain. On examination, she is found to have rashes on the back of her legs, buttocks and the extensor surface of her forearms. Laboratory analysis reveals proteinuria and microscopic hematuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The child's symptoms of cramping abdominal pain, palpable purpuric rashes on the legs, buttocks, and extensor surfaces, along with proteinuria and microscopic hematuria, are classic features of Henoch-Schönlein Purpura (HSP), now known as IgA vasculitis. HSP is a systemic vasculitis characterized by IgA deposition, primarily affecting small vessels in the skin, joints, gastrointestinal tract, and kidneys.

questions.prompt: Cyclopropagative life cycle is defined as the disease agent which undergoes cyclical change and multiplies in the body of the arthropod. This type of life cycle is seen in which of the following disease?
questions.explanation: A cyclopropagative life cycle is defined as a parasite that undergoes both development (cyclical changes) and multiplication inside the vector's body. This exact life cycle occurs with Plasmodium species in mosquitoes, causing malaria.

questions.prompt: A soldier presents to a referral hospital one day after sustaining a high-velocity shrapnel injury to his right thigh. He complains of severe pain at the wound site. On examination, crepitus is present. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of his condition?
questions.explanation: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) following a high-velocity shrapnel wound with severe pain and tissue crepitus is most commonly caused by Clostridium perfringens. This anaerobic bacterium produces gas and toxins resulting in rapid tissue destruction.

questions.prompt: A 27-year-old man came to the clinic with headache, palpitations, sweating. As there is history of renal problems in his brother and father he requests for an abdominal ultrasound which revealed the presence of multiple renal and pancreatic cysts. 24 hours urinary metanephrine was sent which was elevated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The combination of pheochromocytoma (elevated urinary metanephrines with symptoms of headache, palpitations, and sweating) along with multiple renal and pancreatic cysts and a strong family history of renal problems points toward Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease, an autosomal dominant condition.

questions.prompt: A 50-year-old diabetic man presents with a progressive increase in pain in his calf, initially after walking 400 m and later 200m over the last 6 months. He now prefers to sleep in a seated position by hanging his leg to alleviate pain. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: The patient's progressive calf pain, initially with walking (claudication) and later at rest, relieved by hanging the leg, is characteristic of critical limb ischemia. Rest pain, particularly when relieved by dependency (hanging the leg down to improve blood flow by gravity), indicates severe arterial insufficiency and is a hallmark symptom.

questions.prompt: A 32-year-old female, primigravida at term pregnancy, with a known history of fibroid uterus, is being planned for an elective cesarean section for breech presentation. She insists her fibroid be removed with the surgery; however, she is counselled regarding the disadvantages of myomectomy. Which one of the following conditions is an indication to remove in this patient?
questions.explanation: Myomectomy during a cesarean section carries risks like increased blood loss and potential for uterine rupture in future pregnancies. However, a pedunculated subserosal fibroid is attached by a stalk and can often be removed with minimal uterine incision and blood loss, making it the safest type to excise during a C-section if removal is desired.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis is a series of wave-like muscle contractions that move food through the digestive tract. It starts in the esophagus, where wave-like solid motions of the smooth muscle move balls of swallowed food to the stomach. Which factor is responsible for increasing gastric motility?
options: Presence of fatty food in the stomach
Presence of tryptophan in the stomach
Presence of acid in the stomach
questions.explanation: Gastric motility and emptying are regulated by neural and hormonal mechanisms. Distension of the stomach wall activates stretch receptors and local enteric reflexes (gastroenteric reflex), which significantly increases gastric motility and acid secretion.

questions.prompt: A 24-year-old male is brought to the ER after he was hit by a motorbike while he was crossing the road. He sustained injuries over his abdomen visible over his abdomen with bruising. His blood pressure is 88/60 and IV fluids are immediately instituted. A FAST was done and it was positive. Which of the following is the next step in the management of this patient? FAST: (focused assessment with sonography for trauma)
questions.explanation: A trauma patient with abdominal bruising, hypotension (88/60), and a positive FAST exam indicating hemoperitoneum requires immediate surgical intervention via exploratory laparotomy for hemodynamic stabilization.

questions.prompt: A patient with carcinoma endometrium is treated with pelvic external beam irradiation to the whole pelvis. Which of the following organs is most radiosensitive in the pelvic region?
questions.explanation: Among pelvic organs exposed to external beam radiation therapy for gynecological malignancies, the ovaries are extremely sensitive to ionizing radiation, resulting in premature ovarian failure and permanent loss of endocrine and reproductive function at relatively low radiation doses.

questions.prompt: A patient presented to OPD with complaints of fatigue, loss of appetite, constipation, urinary symptoms of kidney stone, and increased urination. The patient has a history of psychiatric disorder; you suspect a case of hyperparathyroidism. Which of the following investigations is useful in this condition?
questions.explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism is most commonly caused by a single parathyroid adenoma. Technetium-99m Sestamibi scintigraphy is the preferred functional imaging modality for preoperative localization of hyperfunctioning parathyroid tissue.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old woman presents with severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia and infertility. A diagnosis of endometriosis was made, and she was posted for laparoscopy surgery. During the procedure, dense pelvic adhesions were seen with the bowel stuck to the fundus and cystic ovaries stuck to each other. What is the next step in managing this patient?
options: Gestrinone to decrease the LH surge
questions.explanation: Severe endometriosis with frozen pelvis, bowel involvement, and chocolate cysts requires surgical correction. Laparoscopic cystectomy and adhesiolysis aim to restore pelvic anatomy, remove endometriomas, and relieve pain while preserving reproductive potential in women desiring fertility.

questions.prompt: A school has a small outbreak were children are showing symptoms like runny nose, cough, fever and skin rash. The doctors identified it as measles outbreak. Which of the following is the correct time to give post exposure measles vaccine?
questions.explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis for measles using the measles vaccine is effective if administered within 72 hours (3 days) of exposure to prevent or modify the severity of the disease.

questions.prompt: A 27 year old woman presented with a malodorous discharge in the vagina which started a week earlier. On examination, Whiff’s test positive and the gram stain shows the presence of clue cells. This infection is commonly treated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bacterial vaginosis is characterized by a malodorous vaginal discharge, a positive Whiff test (amine odor upon adding potassium hydroxide), and the presence of clue cells (epithelial cells stippled with bacteria) on wet mount. The standard first-line treatment is oral or topical metronidazole.

questions.prompt: A 32-year-old traveler was lost in the desert. He was found after 2 days. He says that he has not consumed food or water for more than 24 hours. His vitals were normal. Which of the following part of the kidney must have been the site of maximum water reabsorption in this case?
questions.explanation: Under conditions of severe dehydration and water deprivation, the kidneys reabsorb the vast majority of filtered water to maintain fluid balance. The proximal convoluted tubule is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 65% of filtered water and sodium obligatorily, representing the site of maximum water reabsorption.

questions.prompt: A 45 year old man presents with fever, headache, photophobia, and neck rigidity for the last 2 days. He had undergone a heart transplant one year back and is on immunomodulatory drugs. A lumbar puncture was taken in view of meningitis which showed reduced glucose, increased protein, and increased leukocytes with predominant neutrophils. On microscopy, differential motility was seen, non-motile at 37 degrees and tumbling motility at 25 degrees. What is the most likely organism causing this?
questions.explanation: Listeria monocytogenes is a facultative intracellular gram-positive bacillus that is an important cause of meningitis in immunocompromised patients, such as heart transplant recipients. A key microbiological feature is its characteristic tumbling motility at room temperature (25°C) and reduced or absent motility at 37°C, along with beta-hemolysis.

questions.prompt: A patient with head and neck cancer was told by his oncologist that needs radiotherapy at a total dose of 70 Gy over a 7 week period for his tumor. He was scheduled to receive a dose of 1.8-2Gy per fraction, once daily over 5 days a week, for 7 weeks. What is this type of radiotherapy called as?
questions.explanation: Conventional or regular fractionated radiotherapy refers to administering radiation in standard daily doses (fractions) of 1.8 to 2 Gy per day, given once daily for 5 days a week over a total duration of several weeks to deliver the prescribed total tumor dose.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old female with a history of recurrent headaches presented for further evaluation. On further workup, hemoglobin and total WBC count were normal, while an elevated platelet count was seen. Bone marrow aspiration showed increased megakaryocytes and a JAK2 mutation. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Essential thrombocythemia is a myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by a sustained elevation in platelet count, normal hemoglobin and leukocyte counts, bone marrow biopsy showing increased numbers of large, mature megakaryocytes, and frequent JAK2 gene mutations.

questions.prompt: A 25-year-old patient presents to the surgical OPD with a painless left inguinal reducible mass. On examination cough impulse is positive. After further investigations, the patient is diagnosed with an inguinal hernia. What is the surgical management of this patient?
questions.explanation: A reducible inguinal hernia in an adult patient is definitively managed via hernioplasty, which involves strengthening the posterior wall of the inguinal canal using a mesh (such as the Lichtenstein repair) to prevent recurrence.

questions.prompt: A male infant was brought to the emergency pediatric unit with abdominal distention. There was a history of recurrent urinary tract infections. On examination, he was found to have urinary retention. Imaging showed bilateral hydronephrosis. What could be probable diagnosis of his condition?
questions.explanation: Posterior urethral valves (PUV) are congenital folds in the prostatic urethra that cause urethral obstruction in male infants. They typically present with urinary retention, abdominal distention, recurrent urinary tract infections, and bilateral hydronephrosis on prenatal or postnatal ultrasound.
questions.topic: Disorders of Kidney and Urinary Tract

questions.prompt: A woman presented with sudden onset of dysphagia, dysarthria, and gait ataxia. MRI revealed an acute infarct in the right dorsolateral medulla. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The patient's symptoms of sudden onset dysphagia (difficulty swallowing), dysarthria (difficulty speaking), and gait ataxia, coupled with an acute infarct in the right dorsolateral medulla, are classic for Wallenberg syndrome, also known as lateral medullary syndrome. This syndrome results from ischemia in the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) territory, affecting structures like the nucleus ambiguus, vestibular nuclei, and inferior cerebellar peduncle.

questions.prompt: A 23-year-old farm worker from a remote village was brought to the hospital 8 hours later, following a snake bite at 5 in the morning. The patient complained of headache, blurred vision, tingling sensation around the mouth, dizziness, and vertigo and had multiple episodes of vomiting since the bite. He has signs of respiratory depression and bradycardia (HR<50). The local wound showed mild swelling and blistering. There are no apparent bleeding manifestations. He was administered 10 vials of antivenom. Which of the following is the subsequent step of management?
questions.explanation: The patient's symptoms (headache, blurred vision, tingling, dizziness, vertigo, respiratory depression, bradycardia) and lack of bleeding manifestations, despite 10 vials of antivenom, are consistent with neurotoxic envenomation, likely from a krait or cobra. These symptoms indicate persistent neuromuscular blockade. Neostigmine with atropine is indicated for neurotoxic snake bites to reverse the neuromuscular paralysis by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase.

questions.prompt: The Factories Act, 1948 is a social legislation which has been enacted for occupational safety, health and welfare of workers at workplaces. What is the maximum number of work hours/ week prescribed under the Factories Act?
questions.explanation: Under the Factories Act of 1948 in India, the statutory maximum number of working hours per week for an adult worker is restricted to 48 hours, with provisions for daily limits and mandatory weekly rest intervals.

questions.prompt: A 28-year-old man reported within 6 weeks after sustaining a penetrating accidental injury to his left eye with a wooden stick. On examination, there is a marked diminution of vision in the right eye associated with pain, redness and photophobia. The first sign, the attending doctor can see on a fundus examination if it is a case of sympathetic ophthalmitis is:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic ophthalmitis is a bilateral granulomatous uveitis occurring after penetrating ocular trauma to one eye. The earliest sign visible on slit-lamp or fundus examination in the sympathizing (uninjured) eye is a subtle retrolental flare or cells in the anterior vitreous, representing early breakdown of the blood-ocular barrier.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child was brought to her pediatrician for routine well-child care. Her physical examination is normal except for a systolic murmur and a widely split-second heart sound that does not vary with respiration. She has no family history of heart disease. Which among the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: An atrial septal defect (ASD) is characterized by a left-to-right shunt resulting in right atrial and ventricular volume overload. Clinically, it presents with a systolic ejection murmur across the pulmonary valve (due to increased flow) and a characteristic widely split second heart sound (S2) that is fixed and does not vary with respiration due to constant right ventricular stroke volume.

questions.prompt: A study to determine the association between maternal smoking histories from pregnant women during their antenatal visits and then subsequently assessing the birth weight of their babies soon after delivery. What type of study is this?
questions.explanation: A prospective cohort study identifies a group of exposed individuals (e.g., pregnant women who smoke) and an unexposed comparison group (non-smoking pregnant women), and follows them forward in time to assess the incidence or measurement of a specific outcome (such as infant birth weight).

questions.prompt: There are two patients, A and B. Patient A shows the following facial features: deviation of angle of mouth to the left, right eyelids completely closed, and wrinkling of the forehead on the right side. Patient B shows the following facial features: deviation of the angle of the mouth to the left, the right eyelid is not closed, and no wrinkling of the forehead on the right side. Identify the correct type of facial palsy in both patients:
options: A- right LMN facial nerve palsy B-Left UMN facial nerve palsy
A-right UMN facial nerve palsy B-right LMN facial nerve palsy
A-left UMN facial nerve palsy B-right LMN facial nerve palsy
A-left LMN facial nerve palsy B-right UMN facial nerve palsy
questions.explanation: Upper motor neuron (UMN) facial nerve palsy affects the contralateral lower face because the upper face receives bilateral cortical innervation. Thus, forehead wrinkling and eye closure are preserved on both sides, while the mouth deviates away from the lesion (Patient A). Lower motor neuron (LMN) facial nerve palsy affects all ipsilateral facial muscles, causing loss of forehead wrinkling, inability to close the eye, and mouth deviation (Patient B).

questions.prompt: A woman is diagnosed with an unruptured tubal ectopic. She is admitted for medical management with methotrexate while a strict watch is kept for signs of tubal rupture. An ectopic sac in which of the following parts of the tube is likely to rupture the earliest in case of failed medical management?
questions.explanation: The isthmic portion of the fallopian tube is the narrowest and least distensible part. An ectopic pregnancy implanted here has limited space to grow, leading to earlier rupture compared to other, more distensible segments like the ampulla. Rupture in the isthmus is often more catastrophic due to its proximity to major blood vessels.

questions.prompt: A young man presents with a sudden onset of severe headache, dizziness, breathlessness, and blurring of vision while trekking on a mountain at an altitude of 5000 meters. He is unable to climb any further. Which of the following indicated the development of high-altitude cerebral edema?
